summary: Layer 1B expands the universe around AI data-center photonics capacity. The node appears to be a plausible chokepoint because 800G/1.6T optical links, lasers, photodetectors, InP devices, and optical manufacturing capacity are increasingly tied to hyperscaler bandwidth demand. The cleanest reference names are Coherent and Lumentum, which anchor InP laser/device capacity. The underfollowed lane includes Fabrinet as a manufacturing-capacity and optical assembly beneficiary, and Aeluma as a speculative alternative III-V-on-silicon platform that could matter if native InP capacity remains constrained. Evidence quality is uneven: COHR, LITE, and FN have more commercial exposure; ALMU remains a higher-risk hypothesis requiring proof of revenue conversion, qualified customers, and scalable yields.
